research: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide: Subject + Action + Location + Composition + Style; be specific; control the camera in photographic terms (angle, lens, f-stop like 'shallow depth of field (f/1.8)'); name film/grade ('cinematic colour grading', 'slight grain'); use POSITIVE framing ('empty street' not 'no cars'), so the empty logo area is described as an empty dark area rather than 'no logo'; 9:16 is a supported ratio; references work best with an explicit relationship instruction.
https://dev.to/googleai/getting-the-most-out-of-nano-banana-2-502k — Google AI dev post: Nano Banana 2 is the fast Flash image model; generate options, pick a composition, then upscale.
https://www.leonardo.ai/news/nano-banana-prompt-guide — practitioner guide: clearly state subject, action and context; plain descriptive sentences beat keyword lists.

https://www.provideocoalition.com/creating-bokeh/ — bokeh size comes from long focal length (150-200mm beats 50mm), wide aperture (f/1.2-f/2.8), camera close to the focus plane and the lights as far behind as possible.
https://canon-europe.com/get-inspired/tips-and-techniques/bokeh-photography — fast lenses 50mm and up for background blur; more aperture blades give rounder light circles; city lights after sunset.
https://www.provideocoalition.com/lens_flares_in_after_effects/ — for a flare that follows a car headlight: track a point, put the flare on a solid above the layer, blend Add/Screen.
https://creativecow.net/?p=96399 — the exact 'logo lit by passing headlights' problem: animated gleam across the logo as cars pass (question thread; technique assembled in notes).
https://www.zapsplat.com/the-importance-of-great-sound-effects-in-your-film/ — distance is mostly wet/dry balance: the more reverb relative to dry, the farther away a sound sits.
https://freesound.org/s/425385 — real recordings of car pass-by horns with natural doppler exist (Freesound, CC licences; check each one) so the doppler need not be faked.
attach_reference: no — the reference's strongest elements are two foreground cars with readable TAXI signs, and attached, Nano Banana tends to bring them into the frame, filling the empty centre the logo needs; describing its bokeh palette, inky blacks and long lens keeps the night consistent and leaves the middle clear (if the plate drifts in colour, try a second pass with the reference attached as 'colour and light only, not content').
notes: LOGO LAY-IN (Premiere or After Effects): 1) Put the white logo + name on the plate at roughly 85-90% white so it never clips, centred in the dark area. Start it nearly invisible (opacity ~15%, or a dark grey version) so it reads as 'there in the dark'. 2) The sweep: duplicate the logo layer, apply a soft white-to-warm (very pale amber, ~4500K) linear gradient wipe or a feathered rectangle mask about a third of the logo's width, and animate it from left to right across ~0.8-1.2 s with ease in/out; set that duplicate to Add/Screen with a Glow (radius small, intensity low). The logo should rise to full brightness as the beam passes and settle to ~70%, not back to black. 3) The headlights themselves: a large soft white-yellow radial gradient solid (Add mode) entering from frame left, crossing and exiting right, slightly ahead of the logo sweep; animate its scale up a little as it passes centre. Add one horizontal anamorphic streak (thin stretched ellipse or Optical Flares/AE Lens Flare on a black solid, Screen mode, slightly blue-cyan core) riding the brightest point, 1-2 frames of peak only. 4) Lift the plate under the beam: on the plate, a feathered mask following the same movement with Exposure +1 to +1.5 so the wet tarmac/bricks catch it, and if the plate has wet ground, a flipped, blurred, 15-25% opacity copy of the logo beneath it, revealed only while the beam passes (a reflection on wet road). 5) Finish with a whole-frame warm wash peaking at +0.3 stops as the car passes, slight grain over everything so the logo sits in the photograph, and a 4-6 frame dip as the light leaves. Keep the logo fixed (no zoom) — the light moves, the logo doesn't. HORN: one horn only, not a blast. Use a real pass-by horn recording with natural doppler (or a single short tap, pitch-dropped by about a semitone over its tail to suggest movement). Put it at a distance: high-pass ~200 Hz, low-pass ~5-6 kHz, low level (-22 to -18 dBFS short-term under any music), and more wet than dry through an outdoor/street reverb or short slap delay (~120-180 ms) rather than a room, so it sounds a street away, not inside. Time it to land just as the headlights reach the logo, pan it with the light (left to right), and let its tail decay into a low distant city bed (traffic drone, far-off murmur) that fades out under the end card. Optionally a soft tyre hiss on wet road under the sweep. Two horns, a close horn or a long blare will read as comedy or alarm; one far-off tap reads as 'someone got home'.

prompts.idea: Low angle across wet tarmac, 85mm: the road itself is the empty stage, the first headlight glow grazing in from the left so the sweep in the edit has a source.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic night photograph, a low-angle view across an empty wet city street in the UK, shot on an 85mm lens at f/1.4 with focus on the black tarmac a few metres away. The middle of the frame is a wide, calm area of deep inky black road with only a faint sheen of rain. Far behind, the street melts into big soft round bokeh circles of warm amber street lamps, red tail lights, and a little pink and cyan from distant shop windows, all held in the top third. At the left edge, the first pale glow of an approaching car's headlights just grazes the wet surface. Rich blacks, fine film grain, still and quiet, the moment before the light arrives. Thanks.

prompts.idea: Straight-on to a dark brick wall, 50mm: a flat, frontal surface the logo can sit on as if projected, with a warm spill at the right edge hinting a car about to turn the corner.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic night photograph, straight-on to a plain dark brick wall on a quiet UK side street, shot on a 50mm lens at f/1.8 from across the road. The wall fills most of the frame and sits in near-black shadow, with a broad, smooth, empty area at the centre where the bricks are barely visible. Along the bottom edge, a soft out-of-focus strip of wet pavement catches warm amber and red reflections. Along the top edge, a few large soft bokeh circles of amber and cyan street lamps hang in the dark. A faint warm wash spills across the far right bricks, as if headlights are about to swing round the corner. Moody, deep blacks, subtle film grain. Thanks.

prompts.idea: 200mm telephoto down a long empty street: the most compressed, reference-like bokeh field, with one far-off blurred taxi light on the horizon as the cab that is coming.
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 cinematic night photograph, a long telephoto view at 200mm and f/2, looking down a long empty city street at night from kerb height. Everything distant is compressed and dissolved into a dense field of large, overlapping, soft round bokeh discs in warm amber, red, soft pink and a touch of cyan, gathered in the upper part of the frame. Far off, low on the horizon, one small glowing yellow taxi roof light sits blurred into a soft yellow oval. The centre and lower half of the picture is a broad empty band of dark wet road, almost pure black, holding only a faint glossy reflection of the distant lights. Inky shadows, gentle film grain, hushed late-night stillness. Thanks.
